sections.html:
Just north of Des Moines, in the north-central part of Polk County, Ankeny works as a suburb. I-35 skirts the east edge, and U.S. Route 69 cuts through the middle. Mention the closest main road when you talk to a buyer, since commuters from the Des Moines area tend to ask about I-35 or U.S. 69 before anything else.

Growth has been quick, and Ankeny now ranks fifth in Iowa by population.

YearPopulationType of count
200027,117Census
201045,582Census
201454,598Special census
202067,887Census
202577,833Estimate

The count more than doubled from 2000 to 2020, which means a large share of the housing dates from those years. Those roofs, furnaces and water heaters are reaching the age when replacing them becomes a real question, and that question often nudges an owner toward selling.

The Ankeny Community School District covers most of the city. It is the sixth-largest in Iowa, with nearly 12,000 students and 16 buildings. Saydel and North Polk serve other parts of Ankeny. Since district lines ignore the city limits, run your address through the district's own boundary tools before telling a buyer which schools apply.

Prairie Trail is a large planned development built on a former Iowa State University research plot. The city bought the land in June 2005 for $23.6 million and sold it to a developer in September 2005. The city agreed to invest up to $20 million in basic infrastructure, which gave the district its own streets, utilities and commercial space.

Houses in newer developments such as this one often come with covenants, association dues or special assessments that older houses in the center of town lack. Have the title company pull those records before a closing date is chosen.

Summers are hot and winters cold. A typical year brings about 37 inches of precipitation and about 25 inches of snow, and the records run from 106 degrees Fahrenheit down to minus 34. Houses here live through both ends, so the furnace, air conditioner, roof and sump pump all earn their keep.

When one of them is on its last legs, a cash sale spares you the replacement bill.

sections.h2: What to gather before you contact a buyer
sections.html:
Having a handful of documents ready speeds things up, since the title company can begin the day you say yes.

  • Every owner's name spelled as on the current deed, plus a copy of the deed if you have one.
  • Your most recent property tax statement, which lets the closing agent look for open installments.
  • The lender's name and a rough payoff figure when a mortgage exists.
  • Any homeowner association contact, since newer subdivisions often have one.
  • A list of known problems with the roof, plumbing, electrical or foundation.

Deeds are recorded and tax records kept at the county level, so your parcel lives under Polk County, with no separate Ankeny office to chase.

All owners of record must agree and sign the deed. When an owner has died, the estate must be opened, or the title cleared some other way, before the house can change hands.

In an inherited sale this is typically the slowest stretch, and paying cash does not shorten it. What cash does change is the rest: no lender review, no appraisal appointment and no repair haggling. Heirs scattered across states can sign separately, so no one has to come to Ankeny for the closing.

Let us know who the heirs are, whether a will exists and whether the estate is open. In return we can say what the title company will probably ask for.

sections.h2: From first message to closing day
sections.html:
Most Ankeny sales follow the same path. You begin by sending the address and a plain description of the house. We look it over and write an offer, which you are free to accept or refuse, and you owe nothing either way. On acceptance, a title company opens a file and checks the owners, any mortgage or lien and any open tax installments.

Title work takes some time, and you can keep your moving plans loose in the meantime. With no lender, there is no appraisal to book and no loan committee to wait for. After title clears, you and the buyer pick the closing date. You then sign the deed and the statements the recorder requires, a mortgage payoff and open property tax come out of the price, and the remainder is yours.

Buyers with a mortgage typically bring an appraisal, an inspection report and repair demands. Any of the three can stall a sale or lower the price. Buying with cash as-is leaves them out, which means an old roof, furnace or water heater counts for what it is instead of becoming a bargaining chip.

Honesty is not skipped. Known problems still go into the paperwork accurately, and liens, back taxes and covenant questions from a newer subdivision still have to be cleared. Dealing with them early is what keeps the schedule short.

Take a few minutes to compare what you would walk away with under each option. For a traditional listing, think about the repairs a lender-backed buyer will ask for, the time the house sits on the market, and the utilities and insurance you keep paying while it does. For a cash offer, look at the written price, who pays which closing costs, and the date you can close.

  • Ask for the offer in writing, and read what it says about the condition of the house.
  • Confirm which title company will handle the closing and who the contact is.
  • Ask what happens if title work turns up a lien or an owner nobody mentioned.
  • Make sure every owner on the deed has seen the offer.

None of this takes long, and it protects you whichever way you sell. If something in the paperwork is unclear, ask before you sign, not after.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Ankeny
sections.html:
Because the buyer pays directly and no lender is involved, closing can happen on the date you choose after title work finishes.

  • Describe the house and its condition, including repairs you have put off.
  • Our written offer follows our review, and you decide whether to take it.
  • The title company drafts the deed, the declaration of value and the groundwater hazard statement, or the sentence claiming its exemption, as Iowa law requires.
  • Transfer tax is charged on the part of the price over $500 unless the deed states an exemption.
  • The Polk County Recorder records the deed.

Houses held by an estate or by several owners need every owner's signature. Mention co-owners at the start, because a missing signature is the usual reason a closing slips. If you are moving for a job or have a firm move-out date, say so and the closing can be built around it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Ankeny?
faqs.a: In 2020 the census found 67,887 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 77,833. That makes Ankeny the fifth-largest city in Iowa.
Polk County, in its north-central part, immediately north of Des Moines.

faqs.q: What are the main roads through Ankeny?
faqs.a: I-35 runs along the east side of the city, and U.S. Route 69 passes through the middle.

faqs.q: What school district is Ankeny in?
faqs.a: The Ankeny Community School District covers most of the city, while the Saydel and North Polk districts cover some parts.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Ankeny house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take the home as it stands, so repairs are not required beforehand. Known problems must still be disclosed accurately.
